repo_notes.content: KBM-flow (Go 1.26+, Cobra CLI + embedded web dashboard) maintains a Markdown knowledge repository: scan stores documents in SQLite, analyze asks a local Ollama model for structured suggestions, a human reviews them, and only apply writes repository files.

Architecture: internal/scanner walks the repo and computes hashes + similarity sketches -> internal/frontmatter parses/validates YAML metadata -> internal/analyzer runs deterministic repair, optional fast-model enrichment, and full analysis -> suggestions persist in internal/database (modernc.org/sqlite) -> internal/review applies accepted actions via os.Root-confined writes -> internal/server exposes the loopback HTTP API/dashboard; internal/linkcheck probes external URLs on explicit request.

Key gotcha: scan/analyze/run never mutate repository files — only apply does. The single documented exception is the tool-owned kbm frontmatter block written by check-links; frontmatter.Canonical excises kbm byte-for-byte before hashing so bookkeeping never requeues analysis or invalidates accepted suggestions.

Key gotcha: apply honors .kb-policy.json (missing=allow, deny/invalid blocks), verifies the canonical source hash, uses os.Root-confined atomic writes, and moves deletions to .kbm-trash — never hard-deletes.

Key gotcha: frontmatter kb_policy.no_llm_context: true keeps a document out of every Ollama prompt; a malformed kb_policy fails closed. repository_path must point at one Knowledge Base MCP Server shelf, not the multi-shelf parent.

Three model lanes: ollama_model (full analysis), ollama_model_fast (optional local enrichment), ollama_model_external (opt-in enhanced lane via --external; stamps external_sha256/external_model instead of the local analyzed_* lineage and sends content off-machine — a documented privacy boundary).

Quality gates: make check (gofmt, vet, race tests, build) and make frontend-check (pinned vendored assets, biome, prettier). Tests must use fake generators/local HTTP servers — never a live Ollama or external calls.
See AGENTS.md for full safety rules, architecture boundaries, and conventions; CHANGELOG.md for unreleased changes.
